findings.summary: The diagnose -> compile -> apply -> converge -> re-audit chain is unreachable in production: no diagnostic_pipeline or recovery_sources are wired, and the contracts of T3b (collector), T4a (convergence) and T4b (compiler) do not compose end to end (accepted-map and base-manifest digests, composite conflict sides, a model-authored red oracle the verifier cannot reproduce without git).
R16 has no end-to-end replay proving automatic convergence with both sides' behaviour; test_recovery_conflict_e2e.py proves provenance only.
recovery_preview supplies no ordinary_exhausted, observations, planner_route or evidence_available, so the ordinary-to-recovery handoff never fires.
carry_ancestry is always empty in conflict observations published by the integrator.
The eight-task and one-supplemental-audit limits of the cycle are not enforced in production code.
/flow shows interventions but not the states of recovery cycles.
Dead-code and test-order findings: bt_recovery_preview now has no M5 import; its model-free test runs in a subprocess.
A nested hold destroyed an operator's stop; the stop did not always win.
RUN.healing.json grew without bound from error texts an agent controls.
A forged RUN.interventions.jsonl row broke the plan page and the feed.
A malformed RUN.healing.json silently disabled healing.
Revert restored stale prerequisites and could remove a real or accepted task from a forged case.
An empty attestation key sealed any receipt.
The feed and the page read an unbounded interventions file.
A frozen revision whose application failed could not be reverted.
remediate decided 'foreign hold' from a JSON parse instead of the hold itself.
The local panel did not validate the Host name (DNS rebinding), read unbounded bodies and compared the token in variable time.
Attestation receipts are bound to task, purpose, value and expected text, not to an attempt or a commit: an old receipt keeps settling the same manual check after a rework.
